profile.campus: Chicago, Cook County, Illinois (QTS Chicago campus)
profile.reading:
Per QTS's own site, this Chicago facility sits at 2800 S Ashland Ave, Chicago, IL 60608 on a 30-acre campus near downtown Chicago, planned as a two-building facility at full build-out (the second building was in pre-leasing as of the source fetch); LEED Gold and Energy Star certified, closed-loop water-recirculating cooling; no sqft or MW figure is published.

QTS was founded in 2003 in Overland Park, Kansas, and was taken private in a roughly $10 billion Blackstone Real Estate Income Trust (BREIT)-led acquisition completed August 31, 2021, per Blackstone's own press release; QTS is no longer an independent SEC filer.

QTS positions itself as a "hyperscale-neutral" wholesale and colocation landlord, leasing built data center capacity to enterprise, cloud, and hyperscale tenants rather than operating its own end-user cloud service, a business model it shares with peers such as Digital Realty and CyrusOne. Since Blackstone completed its roughly $10 billion take-private acquisition in August 2021, QTS has continued expanding across multiple US metros rather than slowing development, including major campus filings and expansions in Phoenix (a 750MW, 375-acre Glendale campus acquired for $255.3 million in July 2022) and Dallas-Fort Worth (its two mega-scale Irving and Fort Worth campuses), consistent with the scale of buildout QTS has also pursued in Northern Virginia, Georgia, and Ohio, tracked elsewhere in this registry.

QTS was originally founded in 2003 in Overland Park, Kansas by Chad Williams, and grew through a mix of acquisitions and ground-up construction into a national wholesale/colocation platform before its 2013 IPO as a publicly traded REIT; that public period ended with the 2021 Blackstone take-private deal. QTS's current published portfolio language describes over 30 facilities across North America and Europe on its own site, while Wikipedia gives a somewhat different approximate figure of 28 locations across 16 US states plus two Netherlands sites (Eemshaven and Groningen), a discrepancy this registry notes rather than resolves in favor of either source.

reading.body:
QTS Chicago is a planned two-building campus on 30 acres near downtown Chicago at 2800 S Ashland Ave. The operator publishes no megawatt or square footage figure for this facility, so its scale cannot be determined from QTS's own disclosures. The campus holds LEED Gold and Energy Star certifications and uses closed-loop water-recirculating cooling, qualifying it to host enterprise, cloud, and hyperscale workloads under QTS's wholesale colocation model.

Illinois has 44 mapped data center facilities and only 6 with published capacity figures totaling 236 MW. QTS Chicago does not publish capacity and therefore cannot be ranked against peers in the state by scale; it appears seventh in a ranking that includes only sites with disclosed megawatt figures, a position that reflects the absence of data rather than confirmed size. Without published specifications, this facility's contribution to AI infrastructure in Illinois remains unquantified.

QTS was taken private by Blackstone for approximately $10 billion in August 2021 and continues to expand across multiple US metros including major campuses in Phoenix and Dallas-Fort Worth. The Chicago campus's omission of published power capacity is consistent with a pattern across most of QTS's portfolio, making it impossible to assess whether this site ranks among the grid-constrained assets driving AI scaling or remains a planned facility of unknown materiality to the market.
